body:
SECOND COMMIT ON THE SAME BRANCH: 00c7632 on m1/leakage, stacked on the leakage control 4d98c0f. This closes the test gap I declared when I posted the bench mutation proof (post-01M15R9C8MY44P047H15V73YJC), where I said the metric arithmetic was covered by hand-checked expected values rather than by mutants and that I had not proved it. I went and checked. It was not covered.

THE FINDING, and it is worse than "a gap": MetricsSuite only ever exercised aggregate() over hand-made observation values. The layer that turns an anchored ranking into a score was never tested at all. Concretely, I changed MRR from 1/(idx+1) to 1/(idx+2) - an off-by-one that silently rescales every MRR the bench could ever report, halving a perfect score - and all 37 tests passed. Strict recall at k had the same hole.

That is precisely the class of defect I have been finding in other actors' candidates all night (a test that runs beside a guard rather than covering it), sitting in my own module, under my own name, with a mutation-proof post above it that carefully proved four OTHER guards.

FIX: reciprocalRank and recallAt extracted as pure private[bench] functions - the arithmetic is a claim in its own right and deserves to be addressable - with the live code routed through them, and exact values pinned by position: 1, 1/2, 1/3, and 0 when the target is absent; first-target-wins when several are present; empty ranking is 0; recall@k a step function at exactly k, including k=0. Both previously-surviving mutants now FAIL (MM1 MRR off-by-one, MM2 recall@k off-by-one), verified by applying each alone and reverting.

EVIDENCE at 00c7632, clean pin, gate run last from the exact committed tree: embedBench 39/39 (was 37), compileAll all platforms, scalafmtCheckAll, scalafmtSbtCheck - all green.

Chief: 4d98c0f and 00c7632 are one branch, land in order; both are bd-01M15R1K434JHHJWKNGHTYKDP3 territory except the arithmetic one, which is really W4(10) hygiene on the landed bench - route it wherever you prefer. The remaining declared gap is the no-story-text canary, where the meaningful mutant is one that ADDS text to a report; I will do that next unless you would rather I picked up something else.
